title: De motu vibratorio laminarum elasticarum, ubi plures novae vibrationum species hactenus non pertractatae evolvuntur

deep.reconstruction:
Problem III of E443: a uniform elastic lamina (beam) AB of length a, pinned at both ends by pins (styli) Aα and Bβ. This is the modern simply supported or hinged-hinged Euler–Bernoulli beam. Euler reuses the standing-wave separation from the earlier problems. With Φ = θx/b, the deflection is y = cos(θθt)·(A cos Φ + B sin Φ + C e^Φ + D e^{-Φ}), where b encodes the stiffness-to-mass ratio, so that y'''' = (θ/b)^4 y.

Boundary conditions at A (x = 0):
- The pin gives y(0) = 0, hence A + C + D = 0.
- No bending moment acts there ("nulla vis incurvans"), so y''(0) = 0, hence −A + C + D = 0.
- Together these give A = 0 and C + D = 0.

Pin reaction at A. Euler then computes the transverse reaction E of the pin at A. It equals the previously defined resultant ∫p dx of the elementary inertial forces evaluated at x = 0:
E = −Kcc(θ³/b³) cos(θθt)(−B + C − D).

Shear and moment on the segment AY. He takes the shear integral with the constant fixed so that it vanishes at x = 0:
∫p dx = −Kcc(θ³/b³) cos(θθt)(A sin Φ − B cos Φ + C e^Φ − D e^{-Φ}) + Kcc(θ³/b³) cos(θθt)(−B + C − D).
Differentiating confirms p = −Kcc(θ⁴/b⁴) y, which is the inertial load. Integrating once more, with the same rule that the constant vanishes at x = 0, gives the moment of the elementary forces about Y. That formula is completed on the next page.

Next page (context). Adding the moment of E recovers the elastic bending moment −Kcc y''. Equilibrium then fixes the reaction F at B, and the condition of zero curvature at B follows. These lead to sin ζ = 0 with C = D = 0, i.e. θa/b = nπ: the mode shapes are sines and the frequencies grow as n².

ideas.what: Hinged (pinned) boundary conditions for a vibrating beam: y = 0 and y'' = 0 at the end

deep.surprise_reason: This is the standard, well-documented derivation of the pinned-pinned beam case in E443. It is covered by Truesdell's historical account, and the computations are correct and routine.
